content.intro: This lesson focuses on advanced troubleshooting scenarios and connects the PDF syllabus topics to a small, inspectable example. Work from the intended data model, write down the expected result, then verify syntax and semantics with the target tool.
content.why_it_matters: Advanced Troubleshooting Scenarios matters because structured-data files sit between people, tools, services, and deployment systems. A clear contract and repeatable checks make the result easier to maintain and safer to consume.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Advanced workflows combine data modeling, schema composition, parser portability, transformation pipelines, streaming, canonicalization, and operational documentation. Use specialized features only when their compatibility and security implications are understood.

content_blocks.title: What you will cover
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly addresses: Valid JSON with an invalid application contract. Syntactically valid YAML with an unexpected type. Data lost during conversion.; Duplicate keys. Large-number precision issues. Parser differences across environments. Diagnosing incorrect effective configuration.. Treat each as part of a workflow: define what the data should mean, represent it consistently, and test how the chosen implementation interprets it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Advanced Troubleshooting Scenarios
content_blocks.code:
When output differs from expectations:
1. Minimize the fixture.
2. Capture exact parser/tool version.
3. Separate syntax, schema, and semantic checks.
4. Compare runtime types, not only printed text.
5. Turn the finding into a regression test.
content_blocks.expected_output: A reduced reproducible fixture and a regression test help distinguish a data bug from an implementation/version difference.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Inspect the example and compare it against the lesson concepts. This code block is static-validation: CodeLeaf does not execute arbitrary data parsers or commands in the standard browser preview.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the starting fixture before each test. Change one field, indentation level, parser option, or schema constraint at a time, then compare the result with the prediction.
content_blocks.limitations: This snippet is a reference/example, not evidence that the CodeLeaf browser executes JSON/YAML parsing, shell commands, or Python. Validate locally with a named parser or tool before relying on it.

items.title: 1. State the contract
items.text: Write down the expected root type, required fields, scalar types, and any compatibility assumptions.

items.title: 2. Validate before use
items.text: Parse the document and run the applicable schema or policy checks; syntax success alone is not full correctness.

items.title: 3. Test a boundary
items.text: Include at least one missing, malformed, ambiguous, or unexpected input and record the desired behavior.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Advanced features are useful only when all relevant tools agree on their semantics. Prefer the simplest portable representation that meets the requirement. Confirm implementation-specific behavior against the target parser, tool version, and standards documentation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself

Predict the parsed types/result, change one relevant detail, and record whether the target tool behaved as expected. Include one invalid or boundary case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating readable text as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Syntax and visual formatting cannot establish data types, schema conformance, or application-specific meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse, validate against the intended contract, and test a valid plus an invalid fixture.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming every parser interprets the feature identically.
common_mistakes.why: Format versions, schema choices, library defaults, and product-specific restrictions affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the exact parser/version and test the target environment.

common_mistakes.why: Missing fields, wrong types, duplicate keys, or ambiguous scalars may still break consumers.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep valid, invalid, and boundary fixtures in version control.
